Dan Cox

Republican candidate for Governor / Lt. Governor, Maryland · Challenger

Attorney (constitutional lawyer); former Maryland state delegate

Dan Cox is a Frederick County attorney who represented District 4 in the Maryland House of Delegates from 2019 to 2023 and was the 2022 Republican nominee for governor, losing to Wes Moore. He filed for governor again in January 2026 with Rob Krop as his running mate. Cox won the June 2026 Republican primary with about 43.8% of the vote, ahead of Ed Hale with about 36.1%.

Where Cox stands

Taxes
Pledged at the October 6 debate not to raise taxes if elected. Says Marylanders are 'paying more but getting less' and points to what he counts as 338 tax, toll and fee increases.
Property taxes and housing
Proposes capping increases in the taxable value of homes and eliminating property taxes for homeowners 65 and older. Says this would lower rents and mortgages.
Transportation costs
Proposes lowering vehicle registration fees and temporarily suspending the state gas tax.
Energy and electricity bills
Proposes bringing more power plants online, expanding nuclear energy, and using state energy funds for temporary relief on electric bills.
Data centers
Wants to halt new data center development in Maryland.
State budget
Says he would close the projected $3 billion budget shortfall by cutting spending he calls wasteful, not by raising taxes and fees.
Affordability
Calls affordability an undercovered issue, pointing to the combined effect of taxes, housing costs and energy prices on Maryland families and businesses.
